perspective:
From Christian Mensah’s perspective, he has access to the following information:

- He and Jonathan have been close friends since childhood; Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice.
- Lately, Christian observed Jonathan acting differently and became anxious/suspicious that Jonathan was hiding something important.
- Christian arranged a meeting at their favorite coffee shop and confronted Jonathan about this.
- Jonathan admitted he had been hiding something and was in some trouble, saying he did not want to worry Christian or drag him into it.
- Christian offered to help. Jonathan accepted support/resources and said he needed to find a way out of the situation.
- Christian asked whether the trouble was illegal. Jonathan told him he could not say for sure, might have gotten involved with wrong people, but said he had not done anything illegal himself.
- Christian told Jonathan he would look into it discreetly. Jonathan trusted him to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe Jonathan was being framed and that someone was trying to set him up.
- Christian told Jonathan he had leads but did not yet know who was responsible, and decided to gather evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Later, Christian identified the person behind it and told Jonathan it was someone both of them knew and trusted.
- Christian felt betrayed and decided to confront that person and bring them to justice. Jonathan warned him the person is dangerous but trusted him to do what is right.

Christian does not have access to hidden details, Jonathan’s private thoughts, or facts neither observed nor told to him.
